## 2. Current state (from `data/_aqueduct/state.db`)

**No state rows.** This source has never produced state. If its adapter is built that is a real problem (the health gate calls it `RED-UNRUN`); if not, it is expected (`PENDING — no adapter built`).

> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts/submissions delivered as two whole-file bulk zips with NO date param on the zip endpoint; SEC refreshes them nightly, so gate on a HEAD vintage signal and re-download+rebuild only when changed (not a giant per-period directory like the 13f/insider data sets, so S4 is out; no server-side date filter on the bulk path, so S2 is out). Split out from source_id sec_edgar (now the relational 13f/insider giant) on 2026-06-25 so both products stay managed; no fetcher implemented yet (full-pull-only ingesters).

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: HEAD with descriptive UA on each bulk zip -- https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/xbrl/companyfacts.zip and .../bulkdata/submissions.zip. Confirmed live: both return Last-Modified, ETag, and Content-Length. Store prior ETag/Last-Modified/Content-Length per file and re-download only when any changes; current code does neither (full-pull-only, prints sha256 only).
- `since_param`: n/a (bulk zip path has no date filter; the matrix's option-1 per-CIK delta via edgar/daily-index/* or data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK##########.json would be a future S2-style upgrade, but the implemented/recommended-interim access is the whole-file zip gated on HEAD)
- `out_paths_note`: TWO stages / TWO dirs, and note: clean lands in clean_grouped NOT clean_full. Raw: data/raw/sec_edgar/companyfacts.zip + submissions.zip (~2.9GB) from fetch_sec_edgar_bulk.py. Clean: data/clean_grouped/sec_edgar/<TICKER>.parquet (~17,274 files, ~123M obs) from ingest_sec_edgar.py (clean_full/sec_edgar is empty). Re-parse overwrites all per-ticker parquets but never prunes -> tickers that vanish upstream leave orphan stale parquets.
- `rate_note`: No key, but SEC REQUIRES a descriptive User-Agent or returns 403 (set to 'Econ-Fin Data Library admin@hfdatalibrary.com'). SEC ~10 req/s fair-access limit -- not a constraint for a few large requests. 5 retries/file w/ 10s sleep, 1s gap between files, 120s timeout. Resume hazard: leftover .part is resumed via HTTP Range against the live URL; if upstream rotated the file mid-download the appended bytes corrupt the zip (no post-download integrity test) -- delete .part before any gated re-download.

**refreshed_elsewhere**: 2026-07-29 — THIS SOURCE IS ALREADY UPDATING, just not by the orchestrator. It is refreshed daily by .github/workflows/sec-edgar-daily.yml, which runs tools/refresh_sec_edgar.py. The health gate therefore shows it PENDING ("adapter not built yet"), which is now MISLEADING: nobody should build the fetcher this entry describes, because the work is done.
Why it lives outside the orchestrator: the served payload is one grouped parquet per COMPANY (clean_grouped/sec_edgar/<ID>.parquet — metric/obs_date/value/vintage_date), not the long series_key/obs_date/value shape the Result contract and the generic CSV derive assume. Nothing in updater/ or core/ can even derive its CSVs.
Why a delta rather than the bulk zip this entry proposes: the HEAD vintage signal is real (verified 2026-07-29 — Last-Modified Tue 28 Jul 2026 04:22:35 GMT, strong ETag, 1,390,705,602 bytes), but it moves 1.39 GB and rebuilds 17,276 files to capture one day of filings. EDGAR's daily-index names the filers (28-108/day) and data.sec.gov returns a company's COMPLETE facts in ~0.3s, so a day costs ~200 requests.
NAME COLLISION, read carefully: the CATALOG's source_id `sec_edgar` is THIS product (17,276 companies of XBRL fundamentals). The REGISTRY's `sec_edgar` entry is a different thing entirely — the relational Form 13F + insider data under clean_full/edgar_13f. Same id, two meanings, depending on which store you are looking at.

**No fetcher module** at `updater/strategies/fetchers/sec_edgar_xbrl.py`. If this source is `live: true` the orchestrator will report `PENDING — no adapter built` and skip it forever, however it is scheduled.

**Ingest script(s)**: `.github/workflows/sec-edgar-daily.yml`, `tools/refresh_sec_edgar.py`, `jobs/fetch_sec_edgar_bulk.py`, `jobs/ingest_sec_edgar.py`

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='sec_edgar_xbrl'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source sec_edgar_xbrl --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source sec_edgar_xbrl --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('sec_edgar_xbrl');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source sec_edgar_xbrl
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
